style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm Paul quotes to prove that the whole human race is under sin. It opens with the fool -- not a dunce but a moral fool -- saying in his heart, 'There is no God,' and then it shows what that sentence produces: corruption, abominable deeds, not one doer of good. The LORD Himself leans down from heaven, the way He did before Babel and Sodom, to see whether anyone anywhere has insight or seeks God, and the inspection comes back unanimous: all have turned aside, together they have gone rotten, there is none who does good, not even one. The devourers eat God's people the way they eat bread and never pray -- and then, mid-meal, they are seized with dread, because God is with the generation of the righteous. They had mocked the afflicted man's only plan, which was to trust; the LORD is his refuge. The last verse looks past the wreckage for a salvation that has to come from God's side -- out of Zion -- and promises that when the LORD restores His people, Jacob will exult. Psalm 53 is a second edition of the same poem -- 'God' for 'the LORD' throughout, and a reworked middle verse -- and Romans 3:10-12 quotes it as Scripture's verdict on the race.

1.text: For the choir director. Of David. The fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God.' They have become corrupt; their deeds are abominable; there is no one who does good.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm of David. The fool [nabal] has said [amar] in his heart [leb], There is no God [Elohim]. They are corrupt [shachath -- ruined], they have done abominable works [alilot -- deeds], there is none that does [asah] good [tov].
1.notes: amar nabal be-libbo en Elohim (H559, H5036, H3820, H430): the nabal -- not a simpleton but a moral fool, Nabal of Carmel's name (1 Samuel 25:25) -- says in his heart 'no God': Psalm 10:4's practical atheism, now as a thesis. hishchitu hitivu alilah (H7843, H8581, H5949): they have ruined, they have made abominable, their deeds -- en oseh-tov (H6213, H2896): no doer of good. Paul heads the chain of Scripture that seals his indictment of the race with this psalm (Romans 3:10-12); Psalm 53 is its twin.

2.text: The LORD looked down from heaven on the children of men to see whether there was anyone with insight, anyone seeking God.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] looked down [shaqaph -- leaned over and gazed] from heaven [shamayim] upon the children [ben] of men [adam], to see [raah] if there [yesh] were any that did understand [sakal -- act with insight], and seek [darash] God [Elohim].
2.notes: YHWH mi-shamayim hishqiph al-bene adam (H3068, H8064, H8259, H1121, H120): the LORD LEANED DOWN from heaven upon the children of men -- shaqaph, the verb of looking out a window (Genesis 26:8) -- the same investigative descent, though a different verb, as before Babel (Genesis 11:5) and Sodom (Genesis 18:21). lirot ha-yesh maskil doresh et-Elohim (H7200, H3426, H7919, H1875, H430): to see if there EXISTS one with insight, one seeking God. The search is real; the result is verse 3.

3.text: They have all turned aside; together they have gone rotten; there is no one who does good, not even one.
3.amp: They are all gone aside [sur -- turned away], they are all together [yachad] become filthy ['stinking', alach, the KJV margin]: there is none that does [asah] good [tov], no, not one [echad].
3.notes: ha-kol sar yachdav neelachu (H5493, H3162, H444): ALL have turned aside; together they have gone rotten -- alach, the margin's 'stinking': a rare root, only here, in Psalm 53:3, and in Job 15:16, whose Arabic cousin is used of milk gone sour; en oseh-tov en gam-echad (H6213, H2896, H259): no doer of good -- not even ONE. The verdict of verse 1 confirmed by the inspection of verse 2, and universalized: 'all' and 'not one' are Romans 3:12's words.

4.text: Have they no knowledge, all these workers of iniquity, who eat up My people as they eat bread and do not call on the LORD?
4.amp: Have all the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven] no knowledge [yada]? who eat up [akal -- devour] My people [am] as they eat [akal] bread [lechem], and call [qara] not upon the LORD [YHWH].
4.notes: ha-lo yadeu kol-poale aven (H3045, H6466, H205): do they not KNOW -- all the workers of aven, wickedness? The question reads as God's own -- 'My people' -- and it is incredulous; okhle ammi akhelu lechem (H398, H5971, H3899): they eat My people the way they eat bread -- casually, daily, without a thought -- YHWH lo qarau (H3068, H7121): and do not call on the LORD. Cannibal appetite and prayerlessness in one verse; the two go together.

5.text: There they were in great dread -- for God is with the generation of the righteous.
5.amp: There were they in great fear ['they feared a fear', pachad, the KJV margin]: for God [Elohim] is in the generation [dor] of the righteous [tsaddiq].
5.notes: sham pachadu phachad (H6342, H6343): THERE they feared a fear, the margin's literal -- the verb stacked on its own noun, the Hebrew way of saying the terror was total -- and it comes out of nowhere, in the middle of the meal; ki-Elohim be-dor tsaddiq (H430, H1755, H6662): because God is in the generation of the righteous -- among the very people they were eating. The devourers discover that the bread had a Guardian.

6.text: You would put to shame the plan of the afflicted -- because the LORD is his refuge.
6.amp: You have shamed [bosh] the counsel [etsah -- plan] of the poor [ani -- afflicted], because the LORD [YHWH] is his refuge [machseh].
6.notes: atsat-ani tabishu (H6098, H6041, H954): you would shame the counsel of the afflicted -- mock his plan, which is simply to trust; ki YHWH machsehu (H3068, H4268): because the LORD is his machseh, his shelter -- the mockery is aimed at the one plan that works. The 'because' can be read as the fools' reason for scorn or the psalmist's reason it fails; both are true.

7.text: Oh, that Israel's salvation would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people, Jacob will rejoice, Israel will be glad.
7.amp: Oh that ['Who will give', natan, the KJV margin] the salvation [yeshuah] of Israel [Yisrael] were come out of Zion [Tsiyyon]! when the LORD [YHWH] brings back [shub] the captivity [shebut -- the fortunes] of His people [am], Jacob [Yaaqob] shall rejoice [gil], and Israel [Yisrael] shall be glad [samach].
7.notes: mi yitten mi-Tsiyyon yeshuat Yisrael (H5414, H6726, H3444, H3478): 'who will give', the margin's literal -- the Hebrew idiom of longing -- salvation for Israel out of Zion. be-shub YHWH shebut ammo (H7725, H3068, H7622, H5971): when the LORD turns the captivity of His people -- the restoration formula of Psalm 126:1 and 85:1. yagel Yaaqob yismach Yisrael (H1523, H3290, H8055, H3478): Jacob will exult, Israel be glad. After the universal verdict of verses 1-3 and the devourers of verses 4-6, the psalm ends by looking for a salvation that comes from God's side -- which is Paul's whole argument after he quotes it (Romans 3:21).
